issues.description: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered mutated on a shared object — race condition across concurrent requests
issues.detail: _get_lora_config returns the same TritonLoraConfig instance from model_metadata. _create_trtllm_generate_request flips is_registered=True without a lock. Two concurrent first-requests for the same LoRA will both see False, both load .npy from disk, but only one inflight registration is guaranteed. Worse: a request that loses the race may send lora_task_id without weights to a backend that hasn't cached it yet. Needs a per-LoRA lock and a real 'registered with backend' signal, not an in-process boolean.

issues.description: lora_task_id assignment is non-deterministic and not unique across model repos
issues.detail: lora_task_id starts at 1 and increments per LoRA per call to _parse_lora_configs. Dict iteration order is insertion order in modern Python, but multi_lora.json was hand-written — there's no guarantee the same name maps to the same task_id across restarts, and IDs collide across different base models sharing the function. TRT-LLM caches by task_id; collision means wrong adapter served. Hash the name or assign per-(model,name) deterministically.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: feature + debug prints + exception traceback churn shipped as one diff
issues.detail: This is at least three patches mashed together: (1) the multi-LoRA TRT-LLM support, (2) print(traceback.format_exc()) sprinkled into every router and a stray print(f'backend: {backend}') in the parser, (3) test refactors. The debug prints are not gated, not logging, and will spam stdout in production. Strip them or move to logger.debug. The feature patch should not carry this.

issues.description: Variable shadowing: lora_config_path is reused for two different paths in the same function
issues.detail: lora_config_path is bound to the multi_lora.json path at the top of the loop, then rebound inside the loop body to model.lora_config.npy. The outer binding is only used in vllm branch existence check earlier — but a future reader chasing the variable will hit two meanings in 30 lines. Rename one. Bad taste, easy fix.

issues.description: Silent return None on parse failure hides real errors from operators
issues.detail: The except Exception block prints a traceback and returns None — meaning a malformed multi_lora.json silently disables LoRA listing for the model. A ServerError raised inside the inner loop will propagate (good), but a JSON decode error or missing file becomes invisible-at-startup behavior change. Pick one: fail loud at startup, or log a warning. Don't both print and swallow.

issues.description: Return type annotation lies — says List[tuple[str,str]] but returns List[TritonLoraConfig]
issues.detail: _parse_lora_configs is annotated `-> None | List[tuple[str, str]]` but actually returns List[TritonLoraConfig]. The annotation is stale from the rename. Type checkers and the next maintainer will be misled. One-line fix.

review.summary: The feature works in the happy path, but the patch ships three things at once and hides two real correctness bugs behind a clean-looking diff. The shared-mutable is_registered flag and the non-deterministic lora_task_id assignment are concurrency and correctness hazards that will bite under load. The scattered print(traceback.format_exc()) calls and the debug `print(f"backend: {backend}")` are not production code — strip them. NEEDS-WORK: fix the task_id determinism, lock or remove is_registered, drop the prints, correct the return type annotation, then resubmit. Don't soften the LoRA registration story by relying on a per-process boolean to mirror backend cache state.
